pro.en: Alpha Chicago, a new private school in downtown Chicago serving kindergarten through eighth grade, uses artificial intelligence to teach core subjects.

Pupils spend one to two hours a day at computers on AI programs for maths, science and reading, and the founder says the software can identify what each child knows and does not know, while every child is assigned a guide rather than a teacher.

Guides lead afternoon workshops on public speaking, coding, outdoor education and life skills, and the school says its classes rank in the top 1% on national standardised tests, a claim that comes from the school itself.

Tuition is about $55,000 per child annually, and Liz Gerber of Northwestern University said the model resembles personalised learning, that she hesitates to call it an AI school, and that its cost puts it out of reach of most families.

Alpha Schools operates 22 schools nationwide, and in Chicago 35 students have expressed interest and two have enrolled against a goal of 50 students, an experiment that shows college students how AI may change learning and whose enrollment target is the next thing to watch.

views.view: The founder praises the AI model, while an expert says the school looks like personalized learning and costs too much for most families.

pro.en: European shares retreated on Nov. 6, following steep declines in Asia and on Wall Street. DW reported that doubts over massive AI investments, together with concern about possible curbs after the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, had unsettled global markets.

A sell-off occurs when large numbers of investors dump shares simultaneously, and when they share a common anxiety, markets across several countries can slide in tandem. On this occasion, the central concern was whether the enormous sums being poured into AI would deliver adequate returns. Wall Street is the shorthand for the main US stock market, while Asian markets refers to the equity exchanges across Asia, and prices can lurch quickly once fear spreads from one market to the next.

For students who invest in stocks or funds, developments abroad can feed through to their own accounts. The next questions are whether scepticism about AI spending persists and whether any new restrictions materialise. A drop in prices does not necessarily endure, which is why many investors advise keeping a long-term perspective.

pro.en: Qantas intends to eliminate roughly 850 back-office positions over the coming years, with the bulk of the work shifting to Accenture teams in India while a portion remains in Australia.
The affected functions include finance, people, procurement and marketing, and the first tranche of changes is scheduled for mid-2027.

Chief executive Vanessa Hudson cited unwieldy back-office workflows and the impact of artificial intelligence, although Qantas has not stated that AI has already displaced 850 employees. The Australian Services Union contends that AI is being used as a pretext for moving jobs to India, and says the airline previously assured staff that no offshoring was planned under the Accenture arrangement.

For Korean students, the case illustrates that corporate roles in areas such as finance and human resources can be exposed to AI and offshoring alike. How many positions AI will absorb, versus simply relocate, remains unclear, and attention now turns to how the union and the airline frame the first round of cuts.

pro.en: Web agents, which are AI programs that browse sites and complete forms for users, must draw on private context to complete their tasks, and a new paper proposes GuardianAgentFlow, which screens outgoing web requests before they are transmitted, with the aim of disclosing no more than is necessary.

The framework comprises three components: a restriction check that grounds permission in the user's instruction, a shared protection scope that aligns rewriting with disclosure checking, and feedback grounded in candidate requests that guides revision prior to transmission.

The authors evaluated the approach on web requests carrying human-reviewed intent labels and report improved request-contract success. They say the gains persist with smaller mediation models and that latency is lower than with full-policy reasoning, although the abstract supplies no numerical results.

For students who delegate email or scheduling to AI assistants, privacy is a pressing concern. The paper is posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share new work before peer review. Attention now turns to whether independent teams can corroborate the findings.

sents.en: Students who use AI agents for bookings or orders should know that a good score does not always mean safe behavior.
sents.ko: 예약이나 주문에 AI 에이전트를 쓰는 학생은 점수가 높다고 안전한 건 아님을 알아야 해요.

pro.en: A preprint puts a widely held assumption to the test: that the two standard methods of grading AI agents are interchangeable. Research benchmarks check an agent's end state against a reference answer, but live services lack any such reference, so an LLM judge is asked to read the transcript and rule on it.

The authors ran 2,160 episodes drawn from the airline and retail domains of tau2-bench and logged every write the agents made to the database. Each episode was scored in four ways, one of them a minimal rule-based check involving no model call, and two annotators independently labeled 120 of the episodes.

The judge returned the same verdict on 98.2% of repeated runs, yet its agreement with native scoring reached just 56.2%. In 11 episodes the agent carried out a write that was forbidden; the judge let 10 to 11 of these through, while the rule-based boundary evaluator flagged every one of the 11.

The authors conclude that whichever evaluator is chosen determines the finding. They also report that verification, correction and safe-termination gates made no significant dent in forbidden writes, which showed up in 11.1% of episodes where no gates were used. The work covers a single study across two task domains, so additional testing is warranted.
Students who hand bookings or orders to AI agents should recognize that a high score does not always signal safe behavior. The next question is whether other teams can replicate these results.

views.view: LLM judges agreed with gold-answer scoring only 56.2% of the time and passed 10 to 11 of 11 forbidden writes.

pro.en: Researchers have proposed a framework for real-time optimal power flow, a task that demands rapid and dependable decisions as operating conditions on an electricity network fluctuate.

Since many operator preferences and safety needs are hard to capture as numerical rewards, the method layers occasional judgments from a large language model on top of the usual physics-based reward while the system is trained offline. A selective human-in-the-loop step then inspects and fixes questionable judgments before they steer the learned policy.

In tests on the IEEE 30-bus and 118-bus systems, language feedback made the resulting policy safer than a vanilla TD3 baseline, and expert calibration on top of it produced the best overall performance together with steadier training.

The study is a single academic paper, so its practical value on live power networks remains to be demonstrated. For students of energy or artificial intelligence, it illustrates how human expertise can be combined with language models.

pro.en: Small open-weight models are well suited to private customer-service deployments, yet they lag frontier systems in two respects: they overlook what a written policy demands in a particular situation, and they behave erratically even when they possess the relevant knowledge.

The authors investigate whether such a model can close both gaps using nothing but its own deployment logs and their reference outcomes, with no stronger teacher model. They begin with a Gemma 4 12B agent that retrieves its domain policy from on-demand skills. In each round the model diagnoses failed conversations and writes rules into those skills, retaining a rule only if it clears code checks, a counterexample self-review, a paired retest and a validation gate calibrated to noise. Reinforcement learning then trains an adapter on complete multi-turn conversations.

On the retail and airline domains of τ²-bench, the agent improved after two rounds, gaining 12.5 points in retail and 19.5 points in airline on its first-try score relative to its starting point. The paper suggests that the rules rescue tasks the agent never solved, whereas the trained weights make already-solved tasks reliable.
The findings come from a single paper and await independent confirmation, but they may interest students who hope to build customer-service agents.

views.view: The authors say rules fix tasks the agent never solved, and training makes solved tasks more reliable.

pro.en: A team of researchers has proposed a multi-head quantum neural network, a module built to run on today's noisy quantum hardware and to take the place of transformer blocks within an already trained large language model.

The design splits the hidden neurons into groups called heads, loads each head onto a small qubit register and ties the heads together with constrained classical linear layers. Applied to Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, a module with 145,281 trainable parameters stands in for eight consecutive transformer blocks, accounting for 16.33% of the model's parameters. It uses 2,048 hidden neurons, 32 heads and eight qubits per head. The authors trained it on an exact statevector simulation and then ran the quantum heads on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.

The evidence is sobering for quantum enthusiasts. Ablation experiments suggest that, across fused spans, the classical mixers carry much of the performance, and control versions with the entangler switched off sometimes beat the complete module on held-out perplexity. A classical network with matched parameters stayed a few percent ahead.
This is a single paper and it does not establish a quantum advantage. Researchers will be looking for experiments that single out a clear benefit from the quantum component.

pro.en: A paper posted to the arXiv preprint server introduces SignRot, a technique intended to make large language models more compact and faster to run through quantization.

Quantization shrinks a model by storing its numbers in fewer bits, yet a handful of extreme activation values, known as massive outliers, hamper compact low-bit storage. Rotation techniques built on randomized Hadamard transforms try to spread those values out, but the authors say that when one outlier dominates a token, the rotated data can break into fragments with empty bins, which undercuts uniform quantization.

SignRot locates the channels that carry massive outliers and builds a sign adjustment vector for the Hadamard row, turning a bimodal distribution into a unimodal one that is easier to quantize. Since the outlier pulls the activation mean away from zero, the authors combine the method with asymmetric activation quantization; it demands just one calibration pass and merely simple sign flips at inference.

When the authors applied SignRot to QuaRot, an existing method, it reached a WikiText2 perplexity of 5.88 and an average zero-shot reasoning accuracy of 72.73 on the LLaMA3-70B model, a result they say surpasses SpinQuant.

Smaller models demand less computing power, a consideration for students with limited hardware, though the figures come from the authors' own tests and the authors say the code is available online. The next question is whether other researchers reproduce the gains across additional models.

views.view: The authors say SignRot is a light, drop-in fix that beats SpinQuant on LLaMA3-70B.

pro.en: A new paper describes SkinAdvisor, an AI tool for forecasting sales of skins, the cosmetic items that are a primary revenue stream for modern online games. The authors say decisions on which skins to make, when to release them and how to price them often rely on intuition.

The system is powered by SkinCast, a forecasting model that projects per-day sales trajectories over 180 days for unreleased skins, drawing on player-preference data and relational information linking players, heroes and skins. SkinAdvisor then ranks candidate skins by forecast-based return on investment.

The authors report that the system has been in production for a full release cycle. In offline experiments, SkinCast reduced RMSE by about 20% relative to the strongest baseline and by about 60% relative to classical methods, while stress tests put p99 latency under 8ms.

The authors draw two lessons from deployment: order-of-magnitude accuracy suffices for production decisions, and pretrained embeddings can leak temporal information, which required splitting the data by season.

For students interested in games or data, the case illustrates how AI can inform product planning, although the figures come from the authors' own experiments. The open question is whether the tool performs as well on other games.

issues.title: Study Finds No Clear Racial or Sex Bias in AI Pain Advice, but Big Gaps Between Models

pro.en: Researchers tested whether large language models reproduce racial and sex bias in pain management, since minority patients often receive less pain treatment than White patients and medical AI could copy that pattern. The preprint, posted on arXiv, describes its analyses as exploratory.

In Study 1, four open-weight models assessed six acute-pain cases, each tested for four races and two sexes, with identity either stated or cued only by a name. In Study 2, 24 configurations of 17 models, including GPT-4.1 mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen, answered the same cases along with 50 Q-Pain cases written by clinicians.

No difference survived statistical correction in Study 1, and none of 1,386 comparisons in Study 2 survived the false discovery rate, with pain-severity differences falling within one point on a 0-10 scale. Opioid decisions were bounded less precisely, so they show no detected difference rather than proof of none, and the few differences that survived favoured Black patients.

Models differed far more from one another than between patients, with the reference patient receiving the high opioid dose in 6% to 93% of responses. The authors say fairness audits of clinical AI should report the noise floor and test each deployed configuration.

For students heading into health fields, the choice of model can change the answer, although the findings stem from a single-prompt task. The open question is whether the pattern holds in more realistic settings.

pro.en: A new study scrutinises the datasets behind computer-use agents, which pick up how to operate phone apps from recorded screens and accessibility trees. Since screen readers depend on those very trees, any missing labels in the original apps can be inherited by the agents trained on them.

The authors measured content-description coverage in two Android datasets, Rico, collected in 2017, and AndroidControl, collected in 2024. Across 17,373,614 interface elements, 17.74% of the Rico elements requiring a description carried one, against 57.27% in AndroidControl, a gap of 39.5 percentage points.

Input controls were the least labelled role in both datasets, and placeholder descriptions were five times more likely in the older one. The authors caution that the datasets also differ in app selection and capture method, so the study cannot show how things changed over time.

Resolving 26,205 task actions to the elements they touched, the authors found that among tappable graphics with no text, demonstrations operated described elements 9.0 points more often, which they characterise as a selection effect inside the benchmark.
For students who build apps, accessibility labels serve both people and AI. The open question is whether other datasets show the same pattern.

pro.en: A new study takes up the problem of assessing chatbot-style language-model systems when the people using them are not static. Having seen a response, a user may alter how they phrase requests and which tasks, and how demanding ones, they pose next, so what a model says can feed back into the very prompts on which it is later judged.

The authors introduce two kinds of comparison between models. The common-distribution effect measures performance across one shared pool of prompts, while the induced-distribution effect measures each model on whatever pool of prompts its own users end up generating.

They demonstrate that benchmark testing run offline and live A/B experiments aim at different targets, which means the two approaches can place models in a different order and point toward different deployment choices. The paper also offers a sufficient condition that guarantees both approaches will produce the same ranking.

Within a stylized linear model, adaptive users can inflate the variance of the resulting estimates, and the authors present this adaptivity as a shared root of familiar pitfalls such as reward hacking and novelty effects. Their conclusion is that researchers should track both how well a model performs and how it shifts user behavior.
For students who build or compare AI tools, a single scoreboard may not tell the full story. The open question is whether teams adopt the approach in real product tests.

issues.title: ECB Official Says AI Spending Is Giving Europe's Economy a Lift

pro.en: Philip R. Lane, a member of the ECB's Executive Board, told a Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco symposium on Oct. 30 that although frontier AI models are developed chiefly in the United States and China, their adoption will be a key determinant of European productivity growth, while AI-related spending already provides a significant stimulus to the euro area economy.

Digital investment in the euro area has risen 73 percent in real terms since 2014, lifting its share of GDP from 2.3 percent to 3.3 percent, and firms in an ECB telephone survey reported that AI had added roughly 10 percent to their capital expenditure plans this year, as the proportion of companies citing AI in earnings calls climbed from about 10 percent to about 40 percent.

Rising prices for AI-related goods have contributed to higher goods inflation, but their weight of 3.4 percent in the consumer price index limits the effect on headline inflation, while euro area investors have increased purchases of US tech equities and bonds issued by US firms, and banks anticipate a gradual but sustained rise in loan demand to finance data centres.

For Korean students, the speech illustrates how the AI boom is filtering into employment and investment, as global demand for AI hardware reaches Asian suppliers, and attention will turn to whether the growth in AI lending and funding places strain on the financial system.

issues.gist: The FAA will now use an AI tool called SMART across the whole US airspace system. Airline leaders like it, but the air traffic controllers' union says it was not involved.

pro.en: The Federal Aviation Administration said on Nov. 10 that it would deploy SMART, an AI-driven advisory tool, across the airspace of all 22 air route traffic control centers nationwide, following a rollout that began over the National Capital Region on Sept. 21 and which the agency described as successful.

The cloud-based $875 million system combines weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing data to forecast congestion, and the FAA says it has helped reroute 180 flights, saving an average of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight.

Airline executives, including the chief executives of Delta Air Lines and American Airlines, have voiced support, but the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, which represents more than 15,000 members, said it was not consulted on the design, testing or implementation of the system.

The agency stresses that a team of FAA specialists in Washington validates each recommendation and that local controllers may decline it, since the tool cannot replace controllers or take over an aircraft, though it has yet to show how the system affects passenger traffic.

issues.title: Drone and Missile Strikes on Data Centers Raise New Worries About the Cloud
issues.gist: Strikes on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year have cut cloud services for millions of people. Ars Technica will host a live talk about it on November 17.

sents.ko: 이 공격은 미국과 이스라엘이 이란과 벌인 전쟁 중에 일어났어요.

pro.en: Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, Ars Technica reported, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data.

According to the report, Iranian strikes on Amazon facilities in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran left the company with months of repairs, while Russia and Ukraine have exchanged strikes on each other's data centers.

On Nov. 17 at 1 p.m. Eastern, an Ars reporter will host a live conversation with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, on whether hardening data centers against drones and missiles is realistic and how cloud resilience can be improved in wartime.

Because so many student apps, course files and accounts depend on the cloud, the issue reaches well beyond defense circles, and attention will turn to how governments and cloud providers weigh where to deploy data centers amid growing geopolitical risk.

views.view: Ars says strikes on data centers are a new concern for Big Tech, governments and everyone who relies on the cloud.

issues.title: US Envoys Say Putin Agrees to Let Europe Join the Next Round of Ukraine Peace Talks
issues.gist: After meeting Putin in Moscow, US envoys said Europe will join the next round of Ukraine peace talks. But Putin did not change Russia's main demands, so big gaps remain.
issues.gistKo: 미국 특사들이 푸틴을 만난 뒤 다음 우크라이나 평화 회담에 유럽도 참여한다고 밝혔어요. 하지만 푸틴은 러시아의 핵심 요구를 바꾸지 않아서 큰 차이가 그대로예요.
issues.easyKo: 그동안 평화 회담에는 미국, 러시아, 우크라이나만 앉았어요. 이제 유럽도 자리를 얻을 수 있게 됐지만, 러시아가 전쟁 조건을 바꾸지 않아서 합의까지는 멀어요.

paragraphs.en: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, November 12. Afterward, Witkoff said Putin agreed that European representatives could join the next round of peace talks. He told Russian state TV that Europeans will join at the next meeting. Putin said Washington must work with its European allies to learn if they want peace or war.

sents.en: He told Russian state TV that Europeans will join at the next meeting.

sents.ko: 그는 푸틴이 한번 해 볼 뜻이 있다고 덧붙였어요.

sents.en: The envoys then met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening.

sents.en: Ukraine hopes to join the European Union one day.

No details were given on when it will happen.

sents.en: The fighting has not stopped.

sents.en: The two sides are still far apart on land, security guarantees, NATO and the size of Ukraine's army.
sents.ko: 양측은 땅, 안전 보장, 나토, 우크라이나 군대 규모를 두고 여전히 멀리 떨어져 있어요.

sents.en: Kushner said Russia and Ukraine also agreed on a prisoner swap, the largest of the war.

sents.en: No details were given on when it will happen.

sents.en: Irish leader Micheal Martin told European leaders in Dublin that the war has fundamentally reshaped the region's security.

sents.en: The next thing to watch is what role Europe will really play in the next round.
sents.ko: 다음에 볼 것은 유럽이 다음 회담에서 실제로 어떤 역할을 하느냐예요.

pro.en: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the US envoys, met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, Nov. 12, after which Witkoff said Putin had agreed that European representatives could join the next round of peace talks. Witkoff told Russian state television that the Europeans would take part at the next meeting, even as Putin said Washington must work with its European allies to determine whether they want peace or war.

Kushner said he had stressed to Putin how important it was to have the Europeans at the table, adding that the Russian leader was willing to give it a try. The envoys then met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin that evening, and he welcomed the plan as a way of giving the European Union a voice in the negotiations, given Kyiv's hope of eventually joining the bloc.

The BBC reported that Putin made clear Russia's position, including its territorial demands, had not changed. Reuters described the move as a potential breakthrough that nonetheless underlined how difficult the negotiations could become, while EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said a European delegate showed Moscow now saw Europe as a big player, and doubted that Russia was moving toward a peace deal.

The fighting has continued unabated, with ABC News reporting that Russia launched 123 drones overnight and that one person was killed in Kyiv. The parties remain far apart on territory, security guarantees, NATO and the size of Ukraine's armed forces, although Kushner said they had also agreed on the largest prisoner exchange of the war, for which no timetable was given.

Europeans have long argued that they are central to any settlement on their own continent, and Irish leader Micheal Martin told European leaders gathered in Dublin that Russia's war had fundamentally reshaped the region's security. What role Europe will actually play in the next round is now the central question.

views.view: Japan Times, using Reuters, says Europe's seat could be a breakthrough, but Putin's words show how hard talks may be.

pro.en: Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland announced Thursday that he will seek the post of Senate majority leader, setting up a challenge to Sen. Chuck Schumer of New York, the chamber's top Democrat. Democratic senators will choose the leader, with a vote expected in early December.

Van Hollen said voters in last week's midterm elections had called for change and argued that Democrats need new leadership to answer that call. Describing himself as an underdog, he said the race remained in flux, and he urged Democrats to use the Dec. 11 government funding deadline as leverage against the Trump administration over the Iran war.

Schumer, 75, said he welcomed any discussion about the caucus's future and insisted he has the votes to remain leader, citing the party's 55 seats and counting. Sens. Jacky Rosen, John Fetterman and Brian Schatz are among his backers, while Sen. Bernie Sanders has endorsed Van Hollen. Sen. Angus King likened a change now to dismissing a team's manager just after a championship.

Democrats flipped at least eight Senate seats in the midterms, with one race in Alaska still undecided, and CBS News reported that Schumer is still widely expected to hold his post. Some in his party had criticized him in early 2025 over a maneuver to avert a government shutdown. The leadership vote and the Dec. 11 funding deadline are the next milestones.

talk.answerKo: 밴 홀런은 유권자가 변화를 원했다고 하고, 슈머는 자신이 표를 갖고 있다고 해요. 양쪽 다 일리가 있어요. 지도자는 성과와 당의 목소리를 얼마나 듣는지로 평가해야 한다고 생각해요.

issues.title: Harry Kane Breaks England's Appearance Record Weeks After Winning the Ballon d'Or
issues.gist: Harry Kane played his 126th game for England and broke Peter Shilton's record. He scored the winning penalty in a 2-1 win over Croatia, just after winning the Ballon d'Or.
issues.gistKo: 해리 케인이 잉글랜드 대표팀에서 126번째 경기에 나서 피터 실턴의 기록을 넘었어요. 케인은 크로아티아를 2-1로 이긴 경기에서 결승 페널티킥을 넣었고, 얼마 전에는 발롱도르도 받았어요.
issues.easyKo: 쉽게 말하면, 케인은 이번 가을에 세계 최고 선수 상과 잉글랜드 최다 출전 기록을 연달아 가져간 셈이에요. 승리도 챙겼지만 잉글랜드 수비는 숙제로 남았어요.

paragraphs.en: On Thursday at Wembley, England beat Croatia 2-1 in the Nations League. It was Harry Kane's 126th game for England, and it broke Peter Shilton's long-standing record. After a VAR review, England won a penalty for a shirt pull on Kane. Kane scored it for his 92nd goal for England.
paragraphs.ko: 11월 12일 웸블리에서 잉글랜드가 네이션스리그에서 크로아티아를 2-1로 이겼어요. 해리 케인은 126번째 A매치에 나서 피터 실턴의 오랜 출전 기록을 넘었어요. 비디오 판독 뒤 얻은 페널티킥을 넣어 92번째 국가대표 골도 기록했어요.

sents.en: On Thursday at Wembley, England beat Croatia 2-1 in the Nations League.
sents.ko: 목요일 웸블리에서 잉글랜드가 네이션스리그에서 크로아티아를 2-1로 이겼어요.

sents.en: It was Harry Kane's 126th game for England, and it broke Peter Shilton's long-standing record.
sents.ko: 케인의 잉글랜드 126번째 경기였고, 피터 실턴의 오래된 기록을 깼어요.

sents.en: After a VAR review, England won a penalty for a shirt pull on Kane.
sents.ko: 비디오 판독 뒤 케인의 옷을 잡아당긴 반칙으로 잉글랜드가 페널티킥을 얻었어요.

sents.en: Kane scored it for his 92nd goal for England.
sents.ko: 케인이 그것을 넣어 잉글랜드 92번째 골을 기록했어요.

paragraphs.en: The night was planned around Kane. Shilton, Croatia and Prince William, the FA president, each gave him a tribute or gift. Croatia were stronger early on, but England scored first in the 24th minute. Croatia equalized, and then Kane's penalty decided the game.
paragraphs.ko: 경기 전 행사도 케인을 위한 것이었어요. 실턴, 크로아티아, 윌리엄 왕세자(잉글랜드축구협회 회장)가 각각 선물과 기념을 건넸어요. 전반에는 크로아티아가 더 강했지만 잉글랜드는 24분에 먼저 골을 넣었고, 크로아티아가 동점을 만든 뒤 케인의 페널티킥으로 승부가 갈렸어요.

sents.en: The night was planned around Kane.
sents.ko: 그날 밤은 케인을 중심으로 짜여 있었어요.

sents.en: Shilton, Croatia and Prince William, the FA president, each gave him a tribute or gift.
sents.ko: 실턴과 크로아티아, 잉글랜드축구협회 회장인 윌리엄 왕세자가 각각 헌정이나 선물을 건넸어요.

sents.en: Croatia were stronger early on, but England scored first in the 24th minute.
sents.ko: 초반에는 크로아티아가 더 강했지만 잉글랜드가 24분에 먼저 골을 넣었어요.

sents.en: Croatia equalized, and then Kane's penalty decided the game.
sents.ko: 크로아티아가 동점을 만들었고, 그 뒤 케인의 페널티킥이 승부를 갈랐어요.

paragraphs.en: The record came only weeks after Kane won the Ballon d'Or. He won it for the first time on Oct. 26 at the London Palladium. Last season he scored 73 goals in 65 games for club and country. He is the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. He beat Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to the prize.
paragraphs.ko: 이 기록은 케인이 발롱도르를 받고 불과 몇 주 뒤에 나왔어요. 10월 26일 런던 팔라듐에서 케인은 지난 시즌 클럽과 대표팀에서 65경기 73골을 넣은 공로로 처음 상을 받았어요. 잉글랜드 선수로는 2001년 마이클 오언 이후 처음이에요. 라민 야말과 킬리안 음바페를 제쳤어요.

sents.en: The record came only weeks after Kane won the Ballon d'Or.
sents.ko: 이 기록은 케인이 발롱도르를 받고 불과 몇 주 뒤에 나왔어요.

sents.en: He won it for the first time on Oct. 26 at the London Palladium.
sents.ko: 그는 10월 26일 런던 팔라듐에서 처음으로 이 상을 받았어요.

sents.en: Last season he scored 73 goals in 65 games for club and country.
sents.ko: 지난 시즌 그는 클럽과 나라를 위해 65경기에서 73골을 넣었어요.

sents.en: He is the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.
sents.ko: 2001년 마이클 오언 이후 처음 나온 잉글랜드 수상자예요.

sents.en: He beat Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to the prize.
sents.ko: 그는 라민 야말과 킬리안 음바페를 제치고 상을 받았어요.

paragraphs.en: DW says Kane has been the Bundesliga top scorer for three seasons in a row. In his speech, Kane said his path was not straightforward and he had to go on several loan moves. ESPN praised the record night but worried about England's defense. The back four had never started a match together, and at times it showed. Croatia's goal will be grim viewing for England's defense, ESPN wrote.
paragraphs.ko: DW는 케인이 3시즌 연속 분데스리가 득점왕이라고 전했어요. 케인은 수상 소감에서 쉬운 길로 간 게 아니라 여러 번 임대를 다니며 올라왔다고 말했어요. ESPN은 기록의 밤을 칭찬하면서도 잉글랜드 수비를 걱정했어요. 처음 같이 나선 네 명의 수비수가 맞지 않았고, 크로아티아의 골은 수비에게 괴로운 장면이었다고 했어요.

sents.en: DW says Kane has been the Bundesliga top scorer for three seasons in a row.
sents.ko: DW는 케인이 3시즌 연속 분데스리가 득점왕이라고 전해요.

sents.en: In his speech, Kane said his path was not straightforward and he had to go on several loan moves.
sents.ko: 수상 소감에서 케인은 자기 길이 순탄하지 않았고 여러 번 임대를 다녀야 했다고 말했어요.

sents.en: ESPN praised the record night but worried about England's defense.
sents.ko: ESPN은 기록의 밤을 칭찬했지만 잉글랜드 수비를 걱정했어요.

sents.en: The back four had never started a match together, and at times it showed.
sents.ko: 수비 네 명은 한 번도 함께 선발로 나선 적이 없었고, 때때로 그게 드러났어요.

sents.en: Croatia's goal will be grim viewing for England's defense, ESPN wrote.
sents.ko: ESPN은 크로아티아의 골이 잉글랜드 수비에게는 괴로운 장면일 것이라고 썼어요.

paragraphs.en: Kane's story is a good example of steady effort. He did not go straight to the top. His next milestone is 100 goals for England, and ESPN thinks he will reach it soon. The win also sent England into the Nations League quarterfinals.
paragraphs.ko: 케인의 이야기는 꾸준함을 중시하는 대학생에게 좋은 예가 돼요. 케인은 바로 정상에 오른 게 아니라 임대를 거치며 올라왔어요. 다음 기록은 대표팀 100골이고, ESPN은 곧 도달할 것이라고 봤어요. 잉글랜드는 이 승리로 네이션스리그 8강에 올랐어요.

sents.en: Kane's story is a good example of steady effort.
sents.ko: 케인의 이야기는 꾸준한 노력의 좋은 예예요.

sents.en: He did not go straight to the top.
sents.ko: 그는 바로 정상에 오른 것이 아니에요.

sents.en: His next milestone is 100 goals for England, and ESPN thinks he will reach it soon.
sents.ko: 그의 다음 이정표는 잉글랜드 100골이고, ESPN은 곧 이룰 것이라고 봐요.

sents.en: The win also sent England into the Nations League quarterfinals.
sents.ko: 이 승리로 잉글랜드는 네이션스리그 8강에도 올랐어요.

pro.en: Harry Kane made his 126th appearance for England on Thursday, surpassing Peter Shilton's long-standing record, as England beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley in the Nations League. Kane converted a penalty awarded after a VAR review for a shirt pull, taking his tally to 92 England goals.

The evening was built around Kane, with presentations from Shilton, Croatia and Prince William, the FA president. Croatia were the stronger side early on, but England went ahead in the 24th minute. After Croatia equalized, Kane's penalty settled a tight contest.

The milestone arrived only weeks after Kane won the Ballon d'Or for the first time, at a ceremony at the London Palladium on Oct. 26. He was honored after scoring 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season, becoming the first Englishman to claim the prize since Michael Owen in 2001, ahead of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

DW noted that Kane has finished as the Bundesliga's leading scorer for three consecutive seasons, and he told the ceremony his journey had not been straightforward, with several loan moves along the way. ESPN, while celebrating the night, flagged England's defense, saying the back four had never started together and that Croatia's goal would make grim viewing.

Kane's rise from loan spells to the game's top individual prize offers a template for perseverance. His next target is 100 England goals, a mark ESPN expects him to reach before long, and the victory secured England a place in the Nations League quarterfinals.

talk.q: What can students learn from Harry Kane's career?
talk.qKo: 해리 케인의 경력에서 학생들은 무엇을 배울 수 있을까요?
talk.answer: Kane did not go straight to the top. He went on several loan moves and then won the Ballon d'Or and broke England's appearance record. I think his story shows that steady effort matters more than a fast start.
talk.answerKo: 케인은 바로 정상에 오르지 않았어요. 여러 번 임대를 다닌 뒤 발롱도르를 받고 잉글랜드 최다 출전 기록도 깼어요. 그의 이야기는 빠른 출발보다 꾸준한 노력이 더 중요하다는 걸 보여 준다고 생각해요.

issues.title: US Defense Secretary Gives a Medal to the Guard Who Scolded His Group at Arlington
issues.gist: A guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's group to be quiet. A day later, Hegseth gave the guard a medal.
issues.gistKo: 무명용사의 묘를 지키던 병사가 헤그세스 국방장관 일행에게 조용히 하라고 소리쳤어요. 다음 날 장관은 그 병사에게 훈장을 줬어요.
issues.easyKo: 쉽게 말하면, 엄숙해야 할 현충 시설에서 웃고 떠든 장관 일행을 경비병이 혼냈고, 장관이 그 병사를 오히려 칭찬하며 훈장을 준 일이에요.

paragraphs.en: On Wednesday, after a Veterans Day ceremony, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery. A video shows his group, which included his wife and senior advisers, talking and laughing while they posed for photos. A guard, Specialist Thomas Iglesias, stepped forward and shouted that all visitors must keep silence and show respect.
paragraphs.ko: 수요일 재향군인의 날 행사 뒤, 헤그세스 국방장관 일행이 알링턴 국립묘지의 무명용사 묘 앞에서 웃고 떠들며 사진을 찍었어요. 영상에는 토머스 이글레시아스 병장이 다가와 모두 조용히 하고 예의를 지키라고 외치는 모습이 담겼어요.

sents.en: On Wednesday, after a Veterans Day ceremony, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery.
sents.ko: 수요일 재향군인의 날 행사 뒤, 피트 헤그세스 미국 국방장관이 알링턴 국립묘지의 무명용사 묘를 찾았어요.

sents.en: A video shows his group, which included his wife and senior advisers, talking and laughing while they posed for photos.
sents.ko: 영상에는 부인과 고위 참모들이 포함된 일행이 사진을 찍으며 이야기하고 웃는 모습이 담겼어요.

sents.en: A guard, Specialist Thomas Iglesias, stepped forward and shouted that all visitors must keep silence and show respect.
sents.ko: 경비병 토머스 이글레시아스 병장이 앞으로 나서서 모든 방문객은 침묵하고 예의를 지켜야 한다고 외쳤어요.

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, Hegseth gave Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal for doing his duties at the tomb. He posted photos of the award on X and wrote, “We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist.” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the soldier had correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to keep decorum.
paragraphs.ko: 목요일 헤그세스 장관은 이글레시아스 병장에게 합동복무 표창 훈장을 줬어요. 장관은 X에 사진을 올리고 병사를 칭찬했고, 국방부 대변인도 병사가 정확하고 정중하게 일깨웠다고 말했어요.

sents.en: On Thursday, Hegseth gave Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal for doing his duties at the tomb.
sents.ko: 목요일 헤그세스는 이글레시아스에게 묘에서 임무를 수행한 것에 대해 합동복무 표창 훈장을 줬어요.

sents.en: He posted photos of the award on X and wrote, “We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist.”
sents.ko: 장관은 X에 수여 사진을 올리고 “우리는 군인을 사랑합니다. 우리는 기준을 사랑합니다. 잘했습니다, 병장”이라고 썼어요.

sents.en: Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the soldier had correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to keep decorum.
sents.ko: 국방부 대변인 숀 파넬은 병사가 정확하고 정중하게 모두에게 예의를 지키라고 일깨웠다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: DW said the medal is seen as one of the top awards in the US military and is not usually given to junior enlisted troops. Guards from the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, have watched over the tomb around the clock since 1948. pro.en: Following a Veterans Day observance on Wednesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery. Video showed his entourage, including his wife and senior advisers, talking and laughing as they posed for photographs. Specialist Thomas Iglesias, a sentinel on duty, stepped toward the group and shouted that all visitors must maintain silence and respect.

On Thursday, Hegseth presented Iglesias with a Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the tomb. In a post on X featuring photographs of the ceremony, he wrote, “We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist.” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the soldier had correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.

DW noted that the medal is regarded as one of the military's top honors and is not typically awarded to junior enlisted personnel. Soldiers of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, have kept vigil at the tomb around the clock since 1948. The BBC, citing CBS News, reported that guards commonly admonish visitors, several times a day.

The reprimand came in the same week that an effort to impeach Hegseth over the war with Iran collapsed in Congress. The defense secretary dismissed the impeachment push as a “farce” and a “stunt.” DW characterized him as embattled and under fire over the Iran war.

The episode illustrates how a public official's response to a minor misstep can be scrutinized by millions online. Attention now turns to whether the Pentagon offers further explanation and how the congressional debate over the Iran war unfolds.

pro.en: The 27th Latin Grammy Awards wrapped up in Las Vegas on Thursday night, with the Spanish artist Rosalía taking Album of the Year for Lux, her third victory in the category and, according to the BBC, a first for any woman.

Rosalía left with five trophies in all, as "La Perla" earned both Song of the Year and Best Pop Song, Lux was named Best Alternative Music Album, and "Sauvignon Blanc" took Best Short Form Music Video.

Having opened the ceremony with a medley of her best-known songs, she used her acceptance speech to thank herself for ignoring those who had called her music too strange. Lux was released last year to glowing reviews.

The Puerto Rican reggaeton veteran Daddy Yankee was honored as Person of the Year, receiving a lifetime achievement award from Janet Jackson, while Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh became the first Indian artist to perform at the event. Milo J appeared stunned to win Record of the Year, the BBC reported.
The BBC notes that Lux is also regarded as a favorite when the Grammy nominations are announced next week.

views.view: It calls Rosalía's win historic, saying she is the first woman to take best album three times, and it highlights Daddy Yankee and Diljit Dosanjh.

pro.en: Manchester United on Friday appointed Mauricio Pochettino, 54, as head coach, replacing Michael Carrick, who was dismissed following a dismal start to the campaign, with the Argentine having managed the US men's national team since 2024.

The club sit 18th in the Premier League, a point clear of bottom-placed Crystal Palace, after their worst league start in four decades, having collected one win and eight points from 10 league fixtures and three victories from 15 matches in all competitions.

United struck an agreement with the US Soccer Federation to release Pochettino and his staff once his American commitments conclude, and he will take charge of the US against Haiti before moving, having steered the co-hosts to the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, according to Al Jazeera.

Pochettino becomes the eighth permanent United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson departed in May 2013; the club cited his high-intensity attacking football and his record of developing players, and his first match in charge will be at Anfield against Liverpool on Nov. 22.

pro.en: A three-story mixed-use building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn collapsed into an adjacent construction site just after 4 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11, killing eight people, according to the Fire Department, and leaving at least 17 others injured.

The building was fully occupied by residents while workers excavated in the pit next door; crews combed the rubble overnight with floodlights, drones and K-9 units, and the department ended its search just after 3:30 p.m. Thursday without finding further victims. Two of the dead were children, ages 9 and 10.

The cause remains undetermined, with the Department of Buildings and the NYPD examining why the ground gave way and the Brooklyn District Attorney's Office weighing whether criminal conduct contributed; the developers held active permits for excavation and foundation work, and records show the site had been cited for violations months earlier that were corrected before work resumed in May, though investigators have not determined whether that work was a factor.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was heartbroken that eight New Yorkers had lost their lives and lauded the rescuers, including construction workers who dug victims out, while a full stop-work order remains in effect at the site.
Attention now turns to the investigators' findings and to how the city can protect neighboring buildings when major excavation takes place nearby.

views.view: CBS reported that eight people died, that the cause is under investigation, and that the site had been cited for violations months earlier.
ABC reported that eight victims were identified, including two children, and that rescuers worked until Thursday afternoon.

issues.title: Scientists Report Traces of Blood in a 115-Million-Year-Old Dinosaur Bone
issues.gist: Scientists found tiny shapes like red blood cells in a dinosaur bone from Brazil. Tests also found heme, a part of blood.
issues.gistKo: 과학자들이 브라질의 공룡 뼈에서 적혈구처럼 생긴 작은 구조를 찾았어요. 검사에서는 피의 성분인 헴도 나왔어요.
issues.easyKo: 쉽게 말하면, 1억 1,500만 년 된 공룡 뼈 속에서 피의 흔적이 광물로 바뀐 채 남아 있었다는 연구예요. 화석이 부드러운 조직 흔적도 지킬 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

paragraphs.en: Scientists say they found traces of blood in a dinosaur bone that is 115 million years old. The bone is from a small dinosaur called Aratasaurus museunacionali. It was found in northeast Brazil. The team reported the find in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paragraphs.ko: 과학자들이 1억 1,500만 년 된 공룡 뼈에서 피의 흔적을 찾았다고 밝혔어요. 뼈는 브라질 북동부에서 나온 작은 공룡 아라타사우루스 무세우나시오날리의 것이에요. 연구는 미국 국립과학원 회보(PNAS)에 실렸어요.

sents.en: Scientists say they found traces of blood in a dinosaur bone that is 115 million years old.
sents.ko: 과학자들은 1억 1,500만 년 된 공룡 뼈에서 피의 흔적을 찾았다고 말해요.

sents.en: The bone is from a small dinosaur called Aratasaurus museunacionali.
sents.ko: 그 뼈는 아라타사우루스 무세우나시오날리라는 작은 공룡의 것이에요.

sents.en: It was found in northeast Brazil.
sents.ko: 뼈는 브라질 북동부에서 발견됐어요.

sents.en: The team reported the find in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sents.ko: 연구팀은 이 발견을 미국 국립과학원 회보에 보고했어요.

paragraphs.en: Inside the bone, the team saw tiny shapes that look like red blood cells. The shapes sit only inside the narrow canals that once held blood vessels. The rock around the bone did not have these shapes. That makes it less likely that dirt from outside caused them. Tests also found heme, a part of haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in blood.
paragraphs.ko: 뼈 안에서 연구팀은 적혈구처럼 보이는 작은 모양을 봤어요. 이 모양은 혈관이 지나던 좁은 통로 안에만 있었고 뼈를 둘러싼 퇴적물에는 없었어요. 그래서 밖에서 들어온 오염일 가능성이 낮아요. 검사에서는 산소를 나르는 헤모글로빈의 일부인 헴도 나왔어요.

sents.en: Inside the bone, the team saw tiny shapes that look like red blood cells.
sents.ko: 뼈 안에서 연구팀은 적혈구처럼 보이는 작은 모양을 봤어요.

sents.en: The shapes sit only inside the narrow canals that once held blood vessels.
sents.ko: 그 모양은 한때 혈관이 있던 좁은 통로 안에만 있어요.

sents.en: The rock around the bone did not have these shapes.
sents.ko: 뼈 둘레의 퇴적물에는 이런 모양이 없었어요.

sents.en: That makes it less likely that dirt from outside caused them.
sents.ko: 그래서 바깥에서 들어온 오염 때문일 가능성이 낮아져요.

sents.en: Tests also found heme, a part of haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in blood.
sents.ko: 검사에서는 피 속에서 산소를 나르는 단백질 헤모글로빈의 일부인 헴도 나왔어요.

paragraphs.en: The blood did not stay fresh. Instead, the tiny red cells turned into minerals as the fossil formed. The dinosaur was buried fast in a place with little oxygen, which slowed decay. The team also found amino acids linked to collagen, which is found in connective tissue. The authors say the shapes are most likely real fossil blood cells.
paragraphs.ko: 피가 싱싱한 채로 남은 것은 아니에요. 작은 적혈구가 화석이 되는 동안 광물로 바뀌었어요. 공룡은 산소가 적은 곳에 빨리 묻혀서 썩는 속도가 느려졌어요. 연구팀은 결합 조직에 있는 콜라젠과 관련된 아미노산도 찾았고, 그 모양이 진짜 적혈구 화석일 가능성이 가장 크다고 봐요.

sents.en: The blood did not stay fresh.
sents.ko: 피가 싱싱하게 남은 것은 아니에요.

sents.en: Instead, the tiny red cells turned into minerals as the fossil formed.
sents.ko: 대신 작은 적혈구가 화석이 되는 동안 광물로 바뀌었어요.

sents.en: The dinosaur was buried fast in a place with little oxygen, which slowed decay.
sents.ko: 공룡은 산소가 적은 곳에 빨리 묻혔고, 그것이 썩는 속도를 늦췄어요.

sents.en: The team also found amino acids linked to collagen, which is found in connective tissue.
sents.ko: 연구팀은 결합 조직에 있는 콜라젠과 관련된 아미노산도 찾았어요.

sents.en: The authors say the shapes are most likely real fossil blood cells.
sents.ko: 저자들은 그 모양이 진짜 적혈구 화석일 가능성이 가장 크다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: The team calls it the first direct molecular evidence of dinosaur blood compounds inside such cell-like shapes. It shows that fossils can keep soft tissue for millions of years. The name Aratasaurus points to a 2018 fire at Brazil's National Museum. Watch whether other fossils show the same signs.
paragraphs.ko: 연구팀은 이것이 그런 세포 모양 안에 보존된 공룡 피 성분의 첫 직접적인 분자 증거라고 말해요. 화석이 부드러운 조직을 수백만 년 동안 간직할 수 있다는 것을 보여 줘요. 학명 아라타사우루스는 2018년 브라질 국립박물관 화재를 가리켜요. 다른 화석에서도 같은 흔적이 나오는지 지켜봐요.

sents.en: The team calls it the first direct molecular evidence of dinosaur blood compounds inside such cell-like shapes.
sents.ko: 연구팀은 이것이 그런 세포 모양 안에 있는 공룡 피 성분의 첫 직접적인 분자 증거라고 말해요.

sents.en: It shows that fossils can keep soft tissue for millions of years.
sents.ko: 화석이 부드러운 조직을 수백만 년 동안 간직할 수 있음을 보여 줘요.

sents.en: The name Aratasaurus points to a 2018 fire at Brazil's National Museum.
sents.ko: 아라타사우루스라는 이름은 2018년 브라질 국립박물관 화재를 가리켜요.

sents.en: Watch whether other fossils show the same signs.
sents.ko: 다른 화석에서도 같은 흔적이 나오는지 지켜봐요.

pro.en: Researchers reported that a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone from northeast Brazil, belonging to the small dinosaur species Aratasaurus museunacionali, contains traces of blood, in findings published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Inside the bone, the team identified microscopic structures resembling red blood cells confined to the vascular canals that once carried blood vessels, while the surrounding sediment lacked them, which weakens the case for external contamination, and chemical tests also detected heme, a component of haemoglobin, the protein that transports oxygen in blood.

The blood did not survive in its original form; rather, the minuscule red cells mineralised during fossilisation, as the animal was rapidly buried in a low-oxygen setting that slowed decomposition, and the researchers additionally identified amino acids associated with collagen, concluding that the structures most probably represent authentic fossilised red blood cell remains.

The authors described the result as the first direct molecular evidence of dinosaur blood compounds preserved within cell-like structures, suggesting that fossils can retain soft tissue across millions of years, and the genus name alludes to the 2018 fire at Brazil's National Museum, while it remains to be seen whether other specimens yield similar signatures.

views.view: The authors say the shapes are most likely real fossil blood cells, and the finding gives a rare look at the biology of extinct animals.

pro.en: The United Nations nuclear watchdog said it is increasingly concerned about an Iranian uranium enrichment plant in Isfahan that it has never been permitted to inspect. Iran notified the agency of the facility a day before Israel began striking its nuclear sites in June 2025, and the agency says it does not know the plant's precise location or whether it contains nuclear material.

Tehran initially agreed to a visit, but the inspection was called off when the attacks began the following day. The agency renewed its request in February and was refused, with Iran arguing that acts of aggression and continuing threats had made the normal application of safeguards legally untenable and materially impracticable. A September report noted regular vehicular activity around the entrance to a tunnel complex at Isfahan, as seen in satellite imagery.

The site is significant because the agency believes a large share of Iran's highly enriched uranium was held there. Before the June 2025 strikes, Iran had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade. The agency said its lack of information about the material was a matter of serious proliferation concern that must be rectified with the utmost urgency.

Washington and Israel have said their strikes were intended to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, an ambition Tehran denies, insisting its programme is purely civilian. Since the outbreak of the latest war, Iran has restricted inspectors' access, leaving the agency unable to verify its enriched uranium stockpile, and CBS News reported that Tehran has declined to negotiate with the US until a formal ceasefire takes hold.
The central question now is whether Iran will allow inspectors into Isfahan, since it has so far committed to nothing regarding its uranium stockpile or its enrichment programme.

Al Jazeera says the agency cannot confirm whether the underground plant holds nuclear material and calls for inspections to reopen.

pro.en: Pope Leo XIV, the 71-year-old Chicago-born pontiff, has returned to Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary and bishop, and was greeted by crowds that lined the streets.

The visit is part of a 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, with a six-day Peruvian itinerary that includes the Amazon, the high Andes, Cuzco and Chiclayo. The New York Times reported that he was met by President Keiko Fujimori.

On Thursday, Nov. 12, Leo met six victims of clerical abuse for more than an hour, among them people tied to Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, a lay movement that Pope Francis disbanded in 2025. The Vatican said the pontiff thanked them for their testimony, and he later told bishops that the Church must make "amends" to victims.

Victim Renzo Orbegozo, 50, said survivors are seeking "comprehensive reparation," while the US-based watchdog Bishop Accountability presented a list of 77 Peruvian clergy publicly accused of abusing minors, with its co-director urging "zero tolerance."

Leo also denounced "machismo" before a crowd of about 40,000 and addressed roughly 60,000 young people at a prayer vigil at Lima's national stadium. Observers will now watch how the Church follows through on reparation and prevention.

pro.en: A lightsaber wielded by Darth Vader in two Star Wars films fetched nearly $5 million at auction, selling for $4.875 million on Thursday at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction, which was conducted by Heritage Auctions in the United States.

The prop appeared in The Empire Strikes Back in 1980 and Return of the Jedi in 1983, including the celebrated scene in which Vader says, 'I am your father.' Its hilt was fashioned from a 1950s camera flash attachment.

Heritage Auctions said the result set a world auction record for a screen-used Star Wars prop, surpassing the $3.75 million paid in July for Luke Skywalker's lightsaber and a severed hand prop from The Empire Strikes Back, which the same auction house had sold.

Heritage Auctions offered 27 other Star Wars lightsabers as well, along with material from Episodes I through IX and other films and television shows. For many fans, an object from a celebrated scene amounts to owning a fragment of cinema history.

pro.en: CL, the leader of 2NE1, has signed with the music agency The Black Label, the company said Friday, reuniting with Teddy, the K-pop producer behind the music of her group as well as acts such as Blackpink. The Korea Herald described Teddy as a K-pop maestro.

It marks the first time in roughly seven years that the performer has been affiliated with another agency, after she parted ways with YG Entertainment in 2019 and subsequently managed her own one-person agency, Very Cherry.

The agency said CL was embarking on a new chapter grounded in profound trust in Teddy, with whom she has long made music, and that a new single is slated for release by the end of this year. She issued her first solo studio album, Alpha, in 2021. The agency added that she was preparing for a significant leap in her career, having worked independently for most of the period since leaving YG.
The move gives followers of the K-pop industry another example of an artist changing agencies to chart a new course, and attention now turns to the single due before year's end.

views.view: The report presents the deal as a reunion with Teddy and notes it is CL's first new agency link in about seven years.

issues.title: Spain holds its first general strike in 14 years over high rents and the cost of living

pro.en: Spanish workers staged a general strike on Wednesday for the first time in 14 years, called by the country’s main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Many thousands of workers took part, and there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.

In Madrid, roughly 120,000 demonstrators filled the streets and roads were blocked, while upwards of 50,000 gathered in Barcelona, where hooded individuals torched refuse bins and shattered shop windows as police responded with tear gas. The interior ministry reported dozens of arrests, though a woman who attended the Barcelona protest told the BBC that it had been largely peaceful and even joyful.

According to the property portal Idealista, a 50 square meter apartment in Madrid cost an average of €1,170 a month in October, whereas the average gross monthly wage in Spain is roughly €2,460. Rent therefore swallows close to half of typical earnings, far beyond the 30% share that housing specialists commonly regard as affordable, and a teacher named Olga Domingo called the cost of living unsustainable when set against wages.

Pepe Álvarez of the UGT union characterized turnout as massive, and Unai Sordo of the CC OO union judged it very significant. Spaniards go to the polls on Nov. 29 after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez brought the election forward when parliament declined to approve his housing reform plan, and on this occasion the government and its ministers went so far as to urge workers to join the walkout.

The rent-and-wages squeeze resonates with many university students in Korea, and the strike shows how housing costs can mobilize workers across sectors. Attention now turns to how housing is handled in the Nov. 29 election.

views.view: The BBC says unions called the strike over housing and living costs, and it also reports clashes with police in Barcelona and dozens of arrests.
The New York Times says rising rents and low wages have become central issues in the national election.

issues.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong and Yordan Alvarez win unanimous MVP awards in Major League Baseball
issues.gist: Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong and Astros star Yordan Alvarez each won all 30 first-place votes for MVP. It is the first season when both MVPs and both Cy Young winners were unanimous.

pro.en: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez were named unanimous Most Valuable Players of the National and American Leagues on Thursday night, each collecting all 30 first-place votes.

The 24-year-old Crow-Armstrong, in his fourth big-league season, batted .280 with 45 homers and 41 steals while capturing the Gold Glove and Platinum Glove; after Chicago shifted him to the leadoff spot in mid-May to jolt a sputtering offense, he hit .300 with a .398 on-base percentage and drew 83 walks, compared with 29 a year earlier.

Alvarez came close to the Triple Crown, claiming the batting title at .316 with 42 home runs and 106 RBIs and leading the league in on-base percentage, slugging and OPS, while helping a fading Astros club reach the postseason at 81-81.

The sweep made this the first season in which both MVP winners and both Cy Young winners were unanimous, though Crow-Armstrong, who went 0-for-7 in the playoffs, said he felt he could deliver more in bigger moments.
With the awards handed out, attention now shifts to the offseason, as fans wait to see whether the two stars can repeat their form next year.

views.view: Alvarez hit so well that his team made the playoffs, and Crow-Armstrong was great at bat, on the bases and in the field.
Alvarez joined Aaron Judge and Miguel Cabrera as the only players since 1970 to win an AL batting title with 40 or more home runs.

pro.en: England became the first nation to lift the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup three times on Friday, beating France 50-38 in the final in Wollongong, Australia.

Joe Coyd scored four tries, among them the opening two of the match, while Jack Brown added a hat-trick and Rob Hawkins crossed twice, though France, led by a three-try performance from Dany Denuwelaere, mounted a fierce second-half challenge before England pulled clear.

The BBC described a bruising contest of heavy chair collisions, in which a set of goalposts had to be rebuilt and emotions threatened to boil over, calling it a super advertisement for the wheelchair game, while The Guardian framed the result as an historic defence against great rivals.

The triumph offset the disappointment of England's men's and women's teams, both of whom went out in the group stage, and Hawkins is the first player in any form of rugby league to win three successive Golden Boots, with the team having spoken of a desire to win the trophy rather than defend it.
England and France have met four times since 2022, with each side winning twice, and the final suggests that the rivalry between the sport's two powerhouse nations is likely to stay tight.

pro.en: Arsenal earned a 1-1 draw at Barcelona's Camp Nou on Thursday night in the Women's Champions League, with Frida Maanum putting the visitors ahead in the first half and Caroline Graham Hansen equalizing for the hosts.

Barcelona dominated the match, according to the BBC, with almost 70 percent possession, 24 shots and 11 corners yet only a single goal to show for it, and the result ended the Catalan side's perfect record in this season's competition.

The Guardian said Arsenal dug deep to hold on to the draw, the BBC described a gritty showing that had been too rare this season, and manager Renee Slegers cited grit, resilience and discipline while acknowledging that one point was acceptable even though her side had gone for three.

Arsenal remain unbeaten with seven points from four matches but sit sixth in the Women's Super League, and they face London City Lionesses on Sunday and host Lyon next Thursday before concluding the league phase at Inter Milan in December.

pro.en: Novaya Gazeta shuttered its Moscow office on Monday, saying a campaign of state pressure had left it unable to carry on reporting. Outside the building, staff took down a metal plaque and put up a plastic one reading Novaya Gazeta Lived Here, then laid white carnations, which Russians link with mourning, on top.

Russian authorities had branded the paper a foreign agent and ordered it to vacate its Moscow premises, while banks were barred from handling reader donations, a source of income the outlet had come to rely on after moving entirely online. The New York Times described the closure as emblematic of the Kremlin's erasure of dissenting views, a campaign that has gathered pace since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Co-founder Dmitry Muratov, who shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, said as the office closed that people in Russia who stand for peace had been denied the chance to read what they choose. He urged foreign observers to distinguish between the Russian authorities and the Russian people, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov downplayed the closure as part of a rotational process.

Launched in 1993 and co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev, the paper long scrutinized Russia's powerful, and six of its journalists, among them Anna Politkovskaya, have been killed since its founding. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said last month that the outlet had been killed.

Whether the newspaper will attempt to resume work from outside Russia remains unclear, although reporter Irina Vorobyova said its spirit would endure like a good virus. How Novaya Gazeta continues, if at all, in some form abroad is the question now.

issues.title: NASA's Swift Telescope Falls to Earth After Nearly 22 Years and a Failed Rescue
issues.gist: NASA's Swift space telescope fell back to Earth on Nov. 4 after almost 22 years. A robot sent to lift it to a safer orbit failed first.
issues.gistKo: NASA의 스위프트 우주망원경이 거의 22년 만에 11월 4일 지구로 떨어졌어요. 높이 올려 주려고 보낸 로봇은 먼저 실패했어요.

paragraphs.en: NASA's Swift telescope fell back to Earth on Nov. 4 after almost 22 years in space. The US Space Force said it entered the air above North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7:39 a.m. EST. NASA expected most of it to burn up, though some parts might have survived.
paragraphs.ko: NASA의 스위프트 망원경이 11월 4일 거의 22년 만에 지구로 돌아왔어요. 미국 우주군은 인도네시아 북수마트라 위에서 대기권에 들어왔다고 밝혔어요. NASA는 대부분 타 버릴 것으로 봤지만 일부는 남았을 수 있다고 했어요.

sents.en: NASA's Swift telescope fell back to Earth on Nov. 4 after almost 22 years in space.
sents.ko: NASA의 스위프트 망원경이 거의 22년 만인 11월 4일 지구로 떨어졌어요.

sents.en: The US Space Force said it entered the air above North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7:39 a.m. EST.
sents.ko: 미국 우주군은 동부 표준시 오전 7시 39분에 인도네시아 북수마트라 상공에서 대기권에 들어왔다고 했어요.

sents.en: NASA expected most of it to burn up, though some parts might have survived.
sents.ko: NASA는 대부분 타 버릴 것으로 봤지만 일부 부품은 살아남았을 수도 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Swift launched in 2004, and NASA planned for it to work for only two years. It studied gamma-ray bursts, which are strong flashes of light from exploding stars or crashing neutron stars. It could turn quickly toward a flash and alert other observatories. It also studied black holes, supernovae, comets and asteroids.
paragraphs.ko: 스위프트는 2004년에 발사됐고 원래 2년만 쓸 계획이었어요. 별이 폭발하거나 중성자별이 충돌할 때 나오는 강한 빛인 감마선 폭발을 연구했고, 블랙홀, 초신성, 혜성, 소행성도 관측했어요.

sents.en: Swift launched in 2004, and NASA planned for it to work for only two years.
sents.ko: 스위프트는 2004년에 발사됐고 NASA는 겨우 2년만 쓸 계획이었어요.

sents.en: It studied gamma-ray bursts, which are strong flashes of light from exploding stars or crashing neutron stars.
sents.ko: 폭발하는 별이나 충돌하는 중성자별에서 나오는 강한 빛인 감마선 폭발을 연구했어요.

sents.en: It could turn quickly toward a flash and alert other observatories.
sents.ko: 섬광 쪽으로 재빨리 방향을 돌려 다른 관측소에 알릴 수 있었어요.

sents.en: It also studied black holes, supernovae, comets and asteroids.
sents.ko: 블랙홀, 초신성, 혜성, 소행성도 연구했어요.

paragraphs.en: Swift last looked at the sky on Oct. 20, when it was about 171 miles, or 275 kilometers, above Earth. Drag from thin air made it too low to hold steady, so NASA ended the mission three days later. Since 2024, solar activity has swelled the upper atmosphere and pulled Swift down faster than expected.
paragraphs.ko: 스위프트는 10월 20일 마지막으로 하늘을 봤어요. 약 275킬로미터 높이까지 내려와 얇은 공기의 저항 때문에 망원경을 고정할 수 없었고, NASA는 사흘 뒤 임무를 끝냈어요. 2024년부터 태양 활동으로 대기가 부풀어 더 빨리 내려왔어요.

sents.en: Swift last looked at the sky on Oct. 20, when it was about 171 miles, or 275 kilometers, above Earth.
sents.ko: 스위프트는 지상 약 171마일(275킬로미터)에 있던 10월 20일 마지막으로 하늘을 관측했어요.

sents.en: Drag from thin air made it too low to hold steady, so NASA ended the mission three days later.
sents.ko: 얇은 공기의 저항 때문에 너무 낮아져 안정적으로 버티지 못했고, NASA는 사흘 뒤 임무를 끝냈어요.

In late July, LINK lost two of its three reaction wheels and began to spin out of control. Engineers slowed the spin, but the craft no longer had enough fuel to capture Swift. NASA and Katalyst called off the capture in August, and LINK burned up in September.
paragraphs.ko: 구조 시도는 실패했어요. 로봇 우주선 링크는 스위프트를 잡아 약 600킬로미터까지 밀어 올릴 계획이었지만, 7월 말 회전 바퀴 두 개를 잃고 제어 불능으로 돌았어요. 8월에 계획을 접었고 링크는 9월에 먼저 타 버렸어요.

sents.ko: 카탈리스트 스페이스가 만든 로봇 링크는 스위프트를 잡아 약 373마일(600킬로미터)까지 밀어 올릴 계획이었어요.

sents.en: In late July, LINK lost two of its three reaction wheels and began to spin out of control.

sents.ko: 기술자들이 회전을 늦췄지만 스위프트를 잡을 연료가 부족했어요.

sents.en: NASA and Katalyst called off the capture in August, and LINK burned up in September.
sents.ko: NASA와 카탈리스트는 8월에 포획을 취소했고, 링크는 9월에 타 버렸어요.

paragraphs.en: Now NASA is asking private firms how they might help the Hubble Space Telescope. Hubble is likely to fall back to Earth between 2033 and 2034. NASA sent a Request for Information on Oct. 29, and answers are due Nov. 30. These are ideas being explored, not an approved plan.
paragraphs.ko: 이제 NASA는 허블 우주망원경을 돕는 방법을 민간 기업에 묻고 있어요. 허블은 2033~2034년쯤 대기권에 다시 들어올 수 있어요. 10월 29일 정보 요청서를 냈고 답변 마감은 11월 30일이에요. 아직 확정된 계획은 아니에요.

sents.en: Now NASA is asking private firms how they might help the Hubble Space Telescope.
sents.ko: 이제 NASA는 민간 기업들이 허블 우주망원경을 어떻게 도울 수 있는지 묻고 있어요.

sents.en: Hubble is likely to fall back to Earth between 2033 and 2034.
sents.ko: 허블은 2033년에서 2034년 사이에 지구로 떨어질 가능성이 커요.

sents.en: NASA sent a Request for Information on Oct. 29, and answers are due Nov. 30.
sents.ko: NASA는 10월 29일 정보 요청서를 보냈고 답변 마감은 11월 30일이에요.

sents.en: These are ideas being explored, not an approved plan.
sents.ko: 이것은 검토 중인 아이디어이고 승인된 계획은 아니에요.

pro.en: Nearly 22 years after it reached orbit, NASA's Swift Observatory plunged back through the atmosphere on Nov. 4, entering above North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7:39 a.m. EST, according to the US Space Force. Agency officials expected the bulk of the craft to burn up on the way down but conceded that certain components could have survived.

Swift lifted off in 2004 with a design life of only two years. It was built to study gamma-ray bursts, intense flashes of high-energy radiation tied to collapsing massive stars and merging neutron stars. Because it could swiftly reorient toward a burst and notify observatories worldwide, it also examined supermassive black holes, supernovae, comets and asteroids.

Swift made its final observations on Oct. 20, orbiting about 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth, and NASA ended the mission three days later because atmospheric drag had left the telescope unable to hold steady. Solar activity that has swelled the upper atmosphere since 2024 pulled the observatory down faster than expected.

A commercial robotic spacecraft, LINK, built by Katalyst Space, had been sent to seize Swift and raise it to roughly 373 miles (600 kilometers). In late July it lost two of its three reaction wheels and went into an uncontrolled spin; engineers slowed it, but it lacked the propellant to capture the telescope. NASA and Katalyst cancelled the attempt in August, and LINK burned up in September.

NASA is now soliciting ideas from private companies for the Hubble Space Telescope, which is likely to re-enter between 2033 and 2034. The agency issued a Request for Information on Oct. 29, with responses due Nov. 30, but stressed that the options are under exploration rather than formally approved.

issues.title: MIT-led team gets up to $53 million to build safer weed killers with AI
issues.gist: An MIT-led team will get up to $53 million to design new weed killers with AI. They want herbicides that work on resistant weeds and are safer for people.
issues.gistKo: MIT가 이끄는 팀이 AI로 새 제초제를 설계하려고 최대 5,300만 달러를 받아요. 내성 잡초에도 듣고 사람에게 더 안전한 약을 찾는 게 목표예요.
issues.easyKo: 쉽게 말하면, 잡초가 기존 약에 내성이 생기고 있어서 AI로 새 제초제 후보를 찾아보는 연구예요. 사람 건강에 덜 해로운 약을 만드는 것도 목표예요.

paragraphs.en: A team led by MIT will receive up to $53 million from a U.S. health research agency called ARPA-H. The money will pay for a project to build new weed killers. The project is named PLOW, and it is part of an ARPA-H program called STREAM.
paragraphs.ko: MIT가 이끄는 팀이 미국 보건 연구 기관 ARPA-H에서 최대 5,300만 달러를 받아요. 이 돈으로 새 제초제를 만드는 PLOW 프로젝트를 해요. 이 일은 ARPA-H의 STREAM 사업 중 하나예요.

sents.en: A team led by MIT will receive up to $53 million from a U.S. health research agency called ARPA-H.
sents.ko: MIT가 이끄는 팀이 미국 보건 연구 기관 ARPA-H에서 최대 5,300만 달러를 받아요.

sents.en: The money will pay for a project to build new weed killers.
sents.ko: 그 돈은 새 제초제를 만드는 프로젝트에 쓰여요.

sents.en: The project is named PLOW, and it is part of an ARPA-H program called STREAM.
sents.ko: 프로젝트 이름은 PLOW이고, ARPA-H의 STREAM이라는 사업의 일부예요.

paragraphs.en: More than 1 billion pounds of herbicide are used in the United States every year. Farmers use it to stop weeds from destroying crops. However, some weeds are becoming resistant, so the common chemicals work less well. Herbicides may also raise health risks, and people can be exposed through food and drinking water.
paragraphs.ko: 미국에서는 해마다 10억 파운드가 넘는 제초제를 써요. 농부에게는 도움이 되지만 일부 잡초가 내성이 생기고 있고, 건강 위험도 있을 수 있어요.

sents.en: More than 1 billion pounds of herbicide are used in the United States every year.
sents.ko: 미국에서는 해마다 10억 파운드가 넘는 제초제를 써요.

sents.en: Farmers use it to stop weeds from destroying crops.
sents.ko: 농부들은 잡초가 작물을 망치지 않게 하려고 써요.

sents.en: However, some weeds are becoming resistant, so the common chemicals work less well.
sents.ko: 하지만 일부 잡초가 내성이 생겨서 흔한 약이 덜 잘 들어요.

sents.en: Herbicides may also raise health risks, and people can be exposed through food and drinking water.
sents.ko: 제초제는 건강 위험을 높일 수도 있고, 사람들은 음식과 마시는 물로도 노출될 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: The team will use generative AI to predict new molecules that attack the same plant enzymes as glyphosate. The AI will also look for choices that are cheap to make and unlikely to cause resistance. Another goal is to avoid harm to people and nature. The new chemicals could also help the country depend less on imported phosphorus. Christopher Voigt, who leads the project, says new herbicides are needed because of resistance and supply worries.
paragraphs.ko: 팀은 생성형 AI로 글리포세이트와 같은 식물 효소를 공격하는 새 분자를 예측해요. 싸게 만들 수 있고 내성이 덜 생기며 사람과 자연에 덜 해로운 후보를 찾는 것도 목표예요. 수입 인(phosphorus)에 대한 의존도 줄일 수 있어요.

sents.en: The team will use generative AI to predict new molecules that attack the same plant enzymes as glyphosate.
sents.ko: 팀은 생성형 AI로 글리포세이트와 같은 식물 효소를 공격하는 새 분자를 예측해요.

sents.en: The AI will also look for choices that are cheap to make and unlikely to cause resistance.
sents.ko: AI는 만들기 싸고 내성을 잘 만들지 않는 후보도 찾아요.

sents.en: Another goal is to avoid harm to people and nature.
sents.ko: 사람과 자연에 해를 주지 않는 것도 목표예요.

sents.en: The new chemicals could also help the country depend less on imported phosphorus.
sents.ko: 새 화학물질은 수입 인(원소 phosphorus)에 덜 의존하는 데도 도움이 될 수 있어요.

sents.en: Christopher Voigt, who leads the project, says new herbicides are needed because of resistance and supply worries.

pro.en: A research team led by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has been awarded up to $53 million by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, or ARPA-H, to develop next-generation herbicides. The effort, called Precision Learning for On-target Weed control, or PLOW, falls under the agency's STREAM program.

American farmers apply more than 1 billion pounds of herbicide annually, a tool that curbs crop losses but is losing ground as weeds acquire resistance to the most widely used chemicals. Researchers also note that exposure to such products may raise health risks, with people exposed through food and drinking water.

Using generative artificial intelligence, the team intends to predict compounds that disrupt the same plant enzymes targeted by glyphosate, while optimizing for low synthesis costs, limited resistance risk and minimal harm to people and the environment. Christopher Voigt, who leads the project, said resistance mutations and vulnerable supply chains for herbicide precursors could leave the country short of essential agrochemicals; the work could also lessen reliance on imported phosphorus.

The models are expected to produce billions of candidates, which a second group will screen at high throughput before a third group evaluates the survivors in greenhouse trials. Initial greenhouse results are due by the end of the program's first year, and the team will also engineer microbes designed to degrade agrochemicals before they contaminate food, soil or waterways.

issues.gist: A New York judge refused to let two FIFA companies block UEFA from collecting evidence. UEFA wants to know if FIFA's president did anything wrong with his plan to sell World Cup stakes.

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan rejected requests from two FIFA companies in the United States. They had tried to stop UEFA from getting evidence about FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to bring in private investors. The judge said the companies had no direct and legally protected interest in the case.

paragraphs.en: The plan was called FIFA Forward Enterprise, and it became public in July. Investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a permanent stake of more than 20 percent in a company that would run FIFA's tournaments. FIFA's 211 member federations were offered $20 million each to approve it. After a strong backlash, the plan was dropped within days.
paragraphs.ko: 문제의 계획은 7월에 드러난 FIFA 포워드 엔터프라이즈예요. 투자자들이 42억 달러를 내고 대회를 운영할 자회사의 지분 20퍼센트 넘게를 영구적으로 갖는 내용이었어요. 211개 회원 협회에는 승인 대가로 각각 2천만 달러를 주기로 했어요. 큰 반발이 일자 며칠 안에 계획은 철회됐어요.

sents.en: The plan was called FIFA Forward Enterprise, and it became public in July.

sents.en: Investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a permanent stake of more than 20 percent in a company that would run FIFA's tournaments.

paragraphs.en: UEFA asked the court for evidence in August as part of a wider plan to remove Infantino. It says it will file a criminal complaint in Switzerland if it finds financial wrongdoing. sents.en: UEFA asked the court for evidence in August as part of a wider plan to remove Infantino.
sents.ko: UEFA는 인판티노를 물러나게 하려는 큰 전략의 하나로 8월에 법원에 증거를 신청했어요.

sents.en: It says it will file a criminal complaint in Switzerland if it finds financial wrongdoing.

pro.en: A federal judge in Manhattan, Jeannette Vargas, on Thursday denied motions by two U.S. subsidiaries of FIFA seeking to block UEFA from gathering evidence tied to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to bring in private investors. She wrote that the entities lacked a direct, substantial and legally protectable interest in the proceedings.

The scheme, known as FIFA Forward Enterprise, emerged in July. Investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a permanent stake of more than 20 percent in a subsidiary running FIFA's tournaments, while each of the 211 member federations was offered $20 million to endorse it. The proposal was abandoned within days after a fierce backlash.

UEFA filed for discovery in August as part of a broader effort to oust Infantino, and has said it would lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland should it uncover financial wrongdoing. FIFA responded that the court had not addressed the merits of UEFA's application and that no documents are required to be produced.

The decision clears the way for UEFA to seek records from JP Morgan and the investment firm Thrive Capital, which was to anchor the investor group. The ruling was limited to the FIFA subsidiaries' bid to intervene.

Infantino intends to seek re-election in March, and challengers must declare by Nov. 18. So far only Kohzo Tashima of Japan has entered the race, while UEFA is working to persuade Arsene Wenger, FIFA's head of global development, to stand against him.

pro.en: Kenya on Wednesday began a countdown to declaring the end of its Ebola outbreak after its last confirmed patient was discharged. The 11 remaining contacts under watch also left quarantine after 21 days, and Health Secretary Aden Duale said that, for the first time since the outbreak began, Kenya had no patient under treatment and no contact in quarantine.

Since Kenya reported its first case on Oct. 6, nine people have tested positive and two have died. The index patient was a Kenyan man who had returned from Congo; everyone who subsequently fell ill was already in quarantine before developing symptoms, so no community transmission, spread outside a medical setting, has occurred. In all, 135 people have been monitored.
Kenya's outbreak will be officially declared over on Dec. 23, 42 days after the last case was recorded, provided there are no further positive tests.

The outbreak in Congo, by contrast, continues to spread: the WHO tallied 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths as of Oct. 6, with new cases averaging 72 a day over the preceding week. Even so, fears that the epidemic would race unchecked across Africa have not materialized, and Uganda, which logged 20 cases, declared its own outbreak over in August.

Several countries have imposed travel restrictions. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention requires air passengers to sign a document confirming they have not been in Congo in the previous 21 days, while Kenya has set rules for returning citizens that include 21 days of quarantine and monitoring. Dec. 23 is the date to watch.

views.view: The NYT says the milestone shows African countries have mostly kept the virus from spreading in communities.
The WHO reports that Congo had 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths as of Oct. 6, with new cases still averaging 72 a day.
